paper.title: Topic Detection and Tracking Evaluation Overview
paper.abstract: Describes the evaluation framework for Topic Detection and Tracking, including topic tracking, link detection, topic detection, first-story detection, and story segmentation. These tasks provide early operational measures for deciding whether arriving news items continue an existing event or initiate a new one.
paper.venue: Topic Detection and Tracking: Event-Based Information Organization

paper.title: Cross-document Event Identity via Dense Annotation
paper.abstract: Focuses explicitly on cross-document event identity and densely annotates related document pairs. The study examines full identity and closely related quasi-identity cases, exposing ambiguities that sparse coreference annotation can miss.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 25th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning

paper.title: New event detection and topic tracking in Turkish
paper.abstract: Evaluates new-event detection and topic tracking in a news stream. Incoming documents are assessed for whether they describe a previously unseen event and, for known events, whether they belong to an existing tracked topic.
paper.venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology

paper.title: Incremental clustering and dynamic information retrieval
paper.abstract: Studies clustering when observations arrive dynamically and clusters must be maintained as new points are inserted. The work provides foundational algorithms for incremental cluster maintenance rather than assuming a static batch assignment.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 29th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing

paper.title: Using a sledgehammer to crack a nut? Lexical diversity and event coreference resolution
paper.abstract: Examines how lexical diversity affects event coreference and argues that earlier data can make event identity artificially easy when documents within a topic predominantly describe one seminal event. It introduces additional texts containing different instances of similar event types, making false merges between related but distinct events more visible.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

paper.title: FIRLA: a Fast Incremental Record Linkage Algorithm
paper.abstract: Presents an incremental record-linkage algorithm that updates previously established clusters when new records arrive instead of repeating full batch linkage. The work primarily emphasizes computational efficiency while retaining the underlying identity-linkage operation.
paper.venue: Journal of Biomedical Informatics

paper.title: WEC: Deriving a Large-scale Cross-document Event Coreference dataset from Wikipedia
paper.abstract: Introduces a large-scale English cross-document event-coreference dataset derived from Wikipedia. Unlike datasets restricted to predefined topic clusters, it supports event-identity decisions over a broader document collection and provides a substantially larger training resource.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

paper.title: Privacy preserved incremental record linkage
paper.abstract: Develops privacy-preserving incremental record linkage for adding records to previously linked data. New records may attach to existing clusters or form new clusters when no satisfactory existing match is found, directly reflecting an incremental continue-versus-new decision.
paper.venue: Journal of Big Data

paper.title: Generalizing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution Across Multiple Corpora
paper.abstract: Systematically compares cross-document event-coreference methods across several corpora rather than evaluating only in-domain. It shows that cues important for event identity vary across datasets and that neural models may generalize inconsistently, highlighting the danger of transferring benchmark accuracy directly to a different communication domain.
paper.venue: Computational Linguistics

paper.title: First Story Detection In TDT Is Hard
paper.abstract: Examines first-story detection in Topic Detection and Tracking, where an incoming story must be recognized as the first report of a new event rather than a continuation of an existing one. The study highlights the intrinsic difficulty of this online novelty decision.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

paper.title: Incremental entity resolution on rules and data
paper.abstract: Develops incremental entity-resolution techniques for settings where either data or matching logic changes. Previously materialized resolution results are reused to update match-based, distance-based, and pair-oriented resolutions without recomputing everything from scratch.
paper.venue: The VLDB Journal

paper.title: An incremental graph-partitioning algorithm for entity resolution
paper.abstract: Presents incremental graph partitioning for entity resolution when new references arrive and pairwise similarities may change. Unlike purely greedy attachment, the method can revisit previous decisions when new or contradictory evidence changes the consistency of existing clusters.
paper.venue: Information Fusion

paper.title: Incremental Multi-source Entity Resolution for Knowledge Graph Completion
paper.abstract: Studies incremental multi-source entity resolution as new source entities are added to existing clusters. It combines efficient assignment with repair operations that can correct erroneous prior clustering decisions and reduce dependence on insertion order.
paper.venue: The Semantic Web

paper.title: Improved suffix blocking for record linkage and entity resolution
paper.abstract: Develops improved suffix-based blocking methods for record linkage and entity resolution and considers incremental processing after records are inserted. The approach reduces the comparison space while preserving candidates needed to update identity clusters.
paper.venue: Data & Knowledge Engineering

paper.title: Towards Open World Recognition
paper.abstract: Extends open-set recognition to an open-world setting in which a system must detect unknown classes and later incorporate newly labelled classes. The formulation is relevant to incremental identity systems because it separates recognition of known identities from creation and subsequent learning of new identities.
paper.venue: 2015 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

paper.title: Incremental Entity Resolution from Linked Documents
paper.abstract: Studies entity resolution when linked documents are added incrementally rather than processed once in a static batch. Inter-document references and attribute similarity are used so that only a limited affected subset needs to be reconsidered after new data arrives.

paper.title: Probabilistic linkage of large public health data files
paper.abstract: Applies probabilistic record linkage to large data files using field-level agreement evidence and estimated match and nonmatch probabilities. The method operationalizes evidence-based identity decisions when identifiers are imperfect or inconsistent.
paper.venue: Statistics in Medicine

paper.title: Revisiting Joint Modeling of Cross-document Entity and Event Coreference Resolution
paper.abstract: Introduces a neural joint model for cross-document entity and event coreference. Mention representations combine lexical context with predicate-argument relationships, enabling entity and event identity decisions to reinforce one another across documents.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

paper.title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
paper.abstract: Develops selective classifiers that abstain on difficult observations so prediction risk can be constrained while retaining as much coverage as possible. The approach provides a practical mechanism for refusing low-confidence identity assignments instead of forcing every item into an existing class.

paper.title: Case notion discovery and recommendation: automated event log building on databases
authors: Wil M. P. van der Aalst
paper.abstract: Addresses construction of process-event logs when an appropriate case notion is not already fixed. It generates candidate case notions, correlates events into traces under those notions, and ranks alternatives, making it relevant to inferring case identity from multi-attribute event data.
paper.venue: Knowledge and Information Systems

paper.title: Cross-document Event Coreference Search: Task, Dataset and Modeling
paper.abstract: Formulates event-coreference search: given an event mention, retrieve mentions elsewhere in a large collection that refer to the same event. The task moves beyond predefined document clusters and tests event identity in a retrieval-scale setting.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

paper.title: Cross-Document Event Coreference: Annotations, Experiments, and Observations
paper.abstract: Introduces cross-document event coreference as the problem of identifying descriptions in different documents that refer to the same real-world event. It presents annotations and experiments that establish event identity across document boundaries as a distinct coreference problem.
paper.venue: Coreference and Its Applications

paper.title: Cross-document Event Coreference Resolution based on Cross-media Features
paper.abstract: Addresses cross-document event coreference in multimedia news by combining textual event information with visual evidence from news video keyframes. The work tests whether cross-media evidence can help distinguish mentions of the same real-world event from other event mentions.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 2015 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

paper.title: A Framework for Clustering Evolving Data Streams
paper.abstract: Presents a framework for maintaining clustering information over evolving data streams using compact online summaries and later macro-clustering. It is a general streaming-clustering foundation for tracking cluster evolution, although its clusters are not inherently identity-labelled work matters.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 29th International Conference on Very Large Data Bases

paper.title: Joint Entity and Event Coreference Resolution across Documents
paper.abstract: Presents a joint model for cross-document entity and event coreference. It iteratively constructs clusters and exploits dependencies between entity and event mentions, including predicate-argument relations, so evidence about one type can improve identity decisions about the other.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 2012 Joint Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and Computational Natural Language Learning
